$comment: Ed25519 sibling of man-009 (#176 item 19). The `aid` is the 32-byte little-endian encoding of y = 2. It is less than p, but (y^2 - 1) / (d*y^2 + 1) has no square root modulo p, so RFC 8032 §5.1.3 decoding fails at step 3. The value was chosen this way, not as y >= p, so that every RFC 8032 decoder rejects it. Some libraries (pyca/cryptography over OpenSSL, for example) load these bytes as a public key without decoding them and fail only at verification, which would give MANIFEST_POP_FAILED; RFC-AITP-0001 §5.3 requires the decoding itself. Both signatures are literal dummies of the right shape: no key exists to mint them, and the fixture passes by rejecting before any signature is checked (README, "Structural-rejection fixtures").
description: A Manifest whose `aid` is a 43-character `ed25519` identifier on which RFC 8032 §5.1.3 point decoding fails. The value matches the schema pattern, but RFC-AITP-0001 §5.3 makes it an invalid AID, and RFC-AITP-0003 §5 step 2 decodes the key as part of the structural check. Receivers MUST reject with MANIFEST_INVALID, not MANIFEST_POP_FAILED or MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID.

expected.rationale: y = 2 is below p, and (y^2 - 1) / (d*y^2 + 1) mod p is a quadratic non-residue, so no x exists and the key cannot be decoded (RFC 8032 §5.1.3 step 3). Decoding `manifest.aid` is part of RFC-AITP-0003 §5 step 2, before the step 4 PoP check. A key that decodes but is of small order would instead pass step 2 and fail at the signature steps (RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.7).
